attacks.claim: First-pass scale attack is overstated: each transaction is four short queries, so lock hold time is milliseconds. The 5s statement_timeout would only be reached with a queue of thousands of bookings on one class. Pool queueing under a burst is existing behaviour and not a merge blocker.
attacks.evidence: bookLocked runs 4 short queries inside BEGIN/COMMIT; no long-held work inside the lock.

attacks.claim: A lock-wait or statement timeout would surface as a 500 via next(err). The path is rolled back and the client released, so it is safe, and it is unlikely at this hold time. Optional follow-up: a metric or 503 for timeouts.
attacks.evidence: catch (err) { next(err); } with ROLLBACK and client.release(broken) in bookClass.

attacks.claim: Duplicate and capacity protection rely on every booking insert taking the class row lock. There is no unique partial index on (class_id, member_id) WHERE cancelled_at IS NULL as a backstop. The PR states this is a deliberate no-schema-change scope, so a follow-up is reasonable.
